title: A Real‑World Observational Study to Evaluate the Understandability and Actionability of Patient Educational Materials Among Patients with Crohn’s Disease Switching to BBL’s bUstekinumab
summary:
You have been diagnosed with moderate or severe Crohn’s disease. People with Crohn’s disease are often treated with biologic medicines. These medicines target specific processes in the immune system. Today, biosimilars are also available. Biosimilars are medicines that are highly similar to an existing biologic medicine and have comparable effectiveness and safety. For this reason, doctors may sometimes switch treatment to a biosimilar.

One such biologic medicine contains the active substance ustekinumab. As part of your routine care, your doctor may decide to switch your treatment to Yesintek®, an ustekinumab biosimilar from Biocon Biologics. The decision to switch your treatment is made independently of your participation in this study.

Many patients have questions or concerns before such a switch. We have therefore developed information material and a video that explain the switch and show how to inject Yesintek® yourself.

In this study, we want to find out whether this information is easy to understand and helpful in everyday life. Participants will answer short questionnaires on their smartphones. The study does not change your treatment. The results are intended to help improve the information and support provided to patients during future treatment switches.

interventions.name: • On the day of switching, patients who have decided to switch to BBL’s bUstekinumab will be provided with patient support materials, designed to inform patients about biosimilars and for disease education, prior to the switch. This material will be given to patients by the physician or a physician

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Non-Medical Switch
Participants must meet all the following criteria:
1. Participants ≥ 18 years of age on the day of signing informed consent.
2. Diagnosis of moderate to severe Crohn’s disease, as determined by the investigator.
3. Currently receiving ustekinumab and planned to switch to BBL’s bUstekinumab for non-medical reasons, with the decision to switch made prior to and independently of participation in this study.
4. Able to understand and willing to provide written informed consent using the study Informed Consent Form (ICF). The ICF must be voluntarily signed before any study-specific assessments are performed.

Medical Switch
Participants must meet all the following criteria:
1. Participants ≥ 18 years of age on the day of signing informed consent.
2. Diagnosis of moderate to severe Crohn’s disease, as determined by the investigator.
3. Initiated on ustekinumab as part of a step-up therapeutic strategy following inadequate response, loss of response, or intolerance to corticosteroids and/or immunomodulators, with or without prior anti-TNF exposure.
4. Planned to switch to BBL’s bUstekinumab for medical reasons, with the decision to switch made prior to and independently of participation in this study.
5. Able to understand and willing to provide written informed consent using the study Informed Consent Form (ICF). The ICF must be voluntarily signed before any study-specific assessments are performed.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients who have known hypersensitivity to ustekinumab.
2. Patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding.
3. Patients who are participating in a concurrent interventional clinical study.
4. Patients who have any condition that, in the investigator’s judgment, would interfere with the patient’s safety or study interpretation.
